addresses.name: CAIPoliticsMinister::DoWork
addresses.comment: **Virtual slot 10 - the politics minister's daily tick.** 0x8A1A40 to the bare `ret` at 0x8A1B01; one try block catching luabind::error, whose handler (0x8A1B02) hands the error to ReportLuaError (`LUA Error: ...` in the log) and resumes at the epilogue. In order: `+0x30 countdown = 1` (so CAIAgent::Update calls this again on the very next pass - the throttle is the hour test, not the countdown); then acts only when `(this->country_id (+0x38) + 0x11) % 24 == (gamestate->tick - 0x29C55C0) % 24`, both signed `idiv` remainders - once a game day, in the hour (id + 17) mod 24. Inside: `CGregorianDate::GetDayOfMonth(&gamestate->tick)` (0-based) `% 7 == 0` - the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th of each month - runs CAIPoliticsMinister_FillVacantPosts(this) (0x8A1D40) **before** the Lua; then GetThreadLuaState, Lua_PoliticsMinister_Tick (0x8A2040) fetches the global `PoliticsMinister_Tick`, and LuaCallProxy_PoliticsMinister_CallVoid (0x8A1FC0) calls it with one argument - this minister, pushed as its most derived class - and no result. No test of who plays the country, of in_game or of anything else is in the body: those gates are upstream (ProcessAI, CEU3AI::CreateMinisters, CAIAgent::IsEnabled). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md, section E.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing (0x8A1A40-0x8A1B12) and ehcatches.py 0x8A1A40 (one try, .?AVerror@luabind@@). The weekly test is `call 0x44C5C0` with ecx = gamestate+0xBDC, then the 0x92492493 magic and `sub ecx, edx*7; jne`. Wrong if 0x44C5C0 is not 0-based (its record says 0-based; it subtracts month lengths from the day of year starting at 0).
addresses.revises: The existing comment is right in every step it gives; this adds the catch and its log, that the weekly sub-task is CAIPoliticsMinister_FillVacantPosts and runs on the 1st/8th/15th/22nd/29th (day of month 0-based, % 7), that it runs before the Lua, and that the body itself has no player or in-game gate.

addresses.name: CAIPoliticsMinister_FillVacantPosts
addresses.comment: **The AI's weekly refill of empty cabinet posts, in C++, with no Lua.** 0x8A1D40 to the `ret 4` at 0x8A1FB0; the minister on the stack (DoWork pushes ESI). country = countries[minister->owner (+0x54)->+0x24]. Nothing when the country's ministers vector (+0x618..+0x61C) has 1 slot or fewer. For i = 1 .. count-1: pos = g_government_positions->+0xC[i] (the database built lazily through 0x45BD30); skip unless country->ministers[pos->index (+0x4C)] answers **false** to slot 8 (CMinister's 0xA92590 is `mov al,1`, CNullMinister's 0x592360 `xor al,al` - so only a post holding the null minister is filled). Then over GetCountry(minister tag)->PossibleMinisters (+0x160) in list order, with R = country->ruling_ideology (+0x1140), and 'can take' = pos is in his postings (+0x5C) - **not asked for i == 1 (head of state)**: (1) the first one whose ideology (+0x6C) **is R** and who can take it - stop; (2) otherwise the **last** one whose ideology's group (+0x50) is R's group and who can take it; (3) otherwise the **first** one of any ideology who can take it. A found minister is posted as `new CChangeMinisterCommand(country tag, country id, minister, pos)` (0x54E230) straight onto the country's channel - interface_host (+0xF1C) slot 18, then +0x38 slot 6 - with no clone. Not checked: whether he already holds another post, his dates, the post's isChangeable, the country's ruling party being set (R null would fault at R->+0x50).
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing; the decompile agrees. One caller, 0x8A1AC5 in DoWork (findRefs). The tier order is read off the branch targets 0x8A1F11 (break), 0x8A1ECC (store, continue) and 0x8A1EFD (store only when the candidate is still null, 0x8A1ED0). Slot 8 contents checked with vtable.py CMinister CNullMinister. Wrong if the +0x5C list's node layout is not {position, type, prev, next} (the record's CMinisterPosting says it is).

addresses.name: CCurrentGameState_GetAIRand
addresses.comment: **Lua `CCurrentGameState.GetAIRand()`: one draw on the game state's own MT19937 at +0x124** - `lea eax,[state+0x124]; call MT19937Next` - the generator the AI's CEventScopes, CAIIntel, the wolfpack chooser and the hourly trade roll also use, **not** the global one (g_random_seed) that RunHourlyTick reseeds every hour. MT19937Next's two arithmetic shifts keep bit 31 clear, so the answer is in [0, 2^31-1] and a Lua `math.mod(x, n)` of it is never negative. No lock: the minister ticks run on TBB workers, so the order in which countries take draws from this one state follows the threads. Lazily makes the game state if there is none.
addresses.evidence: Read whole (0x8E9950-0x8E99F3): `lea eax,[esi+0x124]; call 0xAA2B90` at 0x8E99D9. Registered name from luabind.json. The thread remark rests on FINDINGS-ai.md (the TBB pass) and on finding no lock in this body or MT19937Next's record; a lock inside the TBB functor was not looked for.

False when (1) the minister's country is at war (+0xACC) and any country on its enemies list (+0x1008) that is not in exile, owns a province, and has an acting capital, has that acting capital on C's continent (+0x368); or (2) any province adjacent to C (C's path node +0xD4, edges +0x90..+0x94, 0x14 bytes each, the neighbour at +4) is **owned** by the exile (+0x330) and **controlled** by a country whose status toward the exile has a war (+0xE28[exile]->+0x20). Otherwise true. `ret 4`, the tag by reference.
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing (0x8A1B20-0x8A1D39); the decompile agrees. 0x42F100 is GetActingCapitalLocation and 0x417AF0 GetCapitalLocation by their records.

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::IsPreparingWar
addresses.comment: Lua `strategy:IsPreparingWar()`: true when some entry of WarTargets (+0x148) is a target that owns a province or is in exile, is not this strategy's country's puppet (target Overlord != this country), and is not in this country's real faction. Bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: Read off the decompile and checked against the listing's exits (0x8ADDFD, 0x8ADE06): the loop continues on (owned < 1 and not exile) or overlord == us or (faction valid and equal).

addresses.name: CAIStrategy::IsPreparingWarWith
addresses.comment: Lua `strategy:IsPreparingWarWith(tag)`: false when this country is already its enemy (CCountry::IsEnemy), or it owns no province, or it is in exile; otherwise true when it is a target in WarTargets (+0x148). `ret 8`.
addresses.evidence: Read off the decompile; `ret 8` at 0x8ADE77..0x8ADEBC on the listing.

addresses.name: CCountry_SetMobilised
addresses.comment: **What CToggleMobilizationCommand does to the country.** Not mobilised (+0x94 == 0) and asked to mobilise: CCountry_AddTimedModifier(country, `initial_mobilization`, (int)(MOBILIZATION_BONUS_DAYS / 1000.0) days - country block +0x60, 30 in Their Finest Hour; the define as an int made a float, over the double 1000.0, back to a float, truncated) and +0x94 = 1. Mobilised and asked to demobilise: the static modifier `initial_mobilization` found in the modifier database and removed (CCountry_RemoveStaticModifier), +0x94 = 0. The other two cases do nothing. Bare `ret`. One caller, CToggleMobilizationCommand::Execute (0x5514DD).
addresses.evidence: Read whole on the listing (0x507A20-0x507B12): `mov esi,edx` (country), `cmp cl,bl` (the flag), GetDefines()+0xCC +0x60, the double at 0x160A300 read as 1000.0, the string 'initial_mobilization' at 0x15BC4B4, 0x4DFB90 and 0x4DFB00. findRefs --callers: one.

structs.name: CAIPoliticsMinister
structs.comment: The politics minister agent: CAIAgent plus +0x54 the owning CEU3AI (Lua's OwnerAI) and +0x58, set to -1 by the constructor and not read in DoWork or its callees. Made by CEU3AI::CreateMinisters on a 0x5C-byte allocation.
structs.evidence: `push 0x5C; call operator new` before `call 0x8A1920` at 0x888E2D-0x888E3B; the constructor's stores; RTTI: CAIPoliticsMinister derives CAIAgent at offset 0, vftable 0x15EBC2C (VA).

struct_fields.name: countdown
struct_fields.comment: Passes left before slot 10 runs: CAIAgent::Update decrements it and calls slot 10 when it reaches 0. The constructor zeroes it; CAIPoliticsMinister::Enable sets it to 1 + (AI generator % 3); every minister's slot 10 sets it back to 1, so after the first run it runs every pass.
struct_fields.evidence: CAIAgent::Update's `dec` on +0x30 (FINDINGS-ai.md); the store in CAIPoliticsMinister::Enable at 0x8A1A27; `mov dword [esi+0x30], 1` at 0x8A1A6D in DoWork.

struct_fields.name: enabled
struct_fields.comment: What CAIAgent::IsEnabled (slot 8) tests and ProcessAI's agent loop gates on. 0 at construction; set by slot 52 (Enable), which CEU3AI::CreateMinisters calls on every minister right after making it.
struct_fields.evidence: IsEnabled `cmp byte [ecx+0x3C], al`; CAIAgent::Enable `mov byte [ecx+0x3C],1`; CAIPoliticsMinister::Enable at 0x8A199D; the [vftable+0xD0] calls in CreateMinisters (0x8889EF, 0x888AE8, 0x888BE1, 0x888CDD, 0x888E8F).

struct_fields.name: allow
struct_fields.comment: The law's `allow` block, embedded. CLaw::ValidFor evaluates it (slot 6) in a scope of the country asked about.
struct_fields.evidence: CLaw's constructor 0x528F60 writes the CAndTrigger vftable 0x15B589C at [edi+0x54] (0x528FF7); CLaw::ValidFor calls [ [this+0x54] + 0x18 ] with this+0x54.

struct_fields.name: ai_generator
struct_fields.comment: **The AI's MT19937** - 624 words, with its index at +0x9C0 from here, i.e. CGameState +0xAE4 (the field recorded as ai_draws). Drawn by CCurrentGameState_GetAIRand (Lua GetAIRand), CAIPoliticsMinister::Enable, CAIIntel, ExecuteDiploDecisions' scope seed, the hourly AI trade roll and the wolfpack chooser - never reseeded hourly the way g_random_seed is.
struct_fields.evidence: `lea eax,[state+0x124]; call MT19937Next` at 0x8E99D9 and 0x8A1A11; MT19937Next keeps its index at state+0x9C0 (its record). Nothing else is recorded between +0x11C and +0xAE4.

struct_fields.name: ai_generator
struct_fields.comment: The same field as CGameState +0x124 - the AI's MT19937 - repeated because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures.
struct_fields.evidence: As CGameState +0x124; the readers above take it through g_CCurrentGameState.
